overview.text:
Himachal Pradesh is known as 'Dev Bhumi', the land of the gods, for the stone-and-wood temples found in almost every valley. Foreign tourist visits rose 32% in 2024, and the state recorded 18.0 million domestic visits.

In the Kullu valley, Manali is the base for Solang's slopes, the high road over Rohtang Pass and the Atal Tunnel to Lahaul. Down-valley, Naggar Castle has stood since around 1460, and each October Kullu Dussehra brings the valley's deities together at Dhalpur Maidan. The Kalka–Shimla railway is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

images.alt: The green Beas valley north of Manali with snow peaks under a blue sky

overview.text:
Manali, at about 2,050 m in the Beas valley, takes its name from 'Manu-Alaya', the abode of the sage Manu, and is often called the 'Valley of the Gods'. Its best-known shrine is the Hadimba Devi Temple of 1553, in a cedar forest above town; Old Manali has the Manu Temple and relaxed cafés, and Vashisht's hot springs are 3 km away.

Manali is also the region's adventure base: skiing and paragliding at Solang Valley, 13 km away; the Hampta Pass trek; and the high road to Rohtang Pass, 51 km away, which needs a permit. The 9.02-km Atal Tunnel, opened in 2020, runs beneath the pass to Lahaul.

best_time.text: Snow falls mainly from December to early March — the time for snow at Solang. The road over Rohtang Pass is usually open from about May to November. For Solang, Incredible India suggests April to June and September to January.

how_to_reach.text: The nearest airport is Kullu–Manali airport at Bhuntar; Kullu itself is about 40 km down the valley. Buses are run by HRTC, HPTDC and private operators.

places.name: Hadimba Devi Temple
places.summary: Manali's pagoda-roofed wooden temple of 1553, in a cedar forest.
places.seoTitle: Hadimba Devi Temple, Manali: History & Visiting
places.seoDescription: Visit the Hadimba Devi Temple in Manali: its 1553 pagoda-style architecture, the Mahabharata legend, carvings, festivals and the cedar forest around it.

images.alt: The tiered wooden roofs of the Hadimba Devi Temple among tall cedars, Manali
images.caption: Hadimba Devi Temple

overview.text: Built in 1553 by Maharaja Bahadur Singh, the Hadimba Devi Temple stands in the Dhungiri cedar forest just above Manali. It honours Hidimba, the wife of Bhima in the Mahabharata, who is worshipped locally as the protector of the valley. The 24-m temple has three square roofs of timber tiles topped by a brass cone. Its carved doorway shows Durga, scenes from Krishna's life and the Navagrahas; inside, a great rock bears the goddess's footprints. A fair is held each May on Hidimba's birthday.

places.name: Solang Valley
places.summary: Manali's playground: skiing in winter, paragliding and a ropeway in summer.
places.seoTitle: Solang Valley, Manali: Skiing, Paragliding & Best Time
places.seoDescription: Solang Valley near Manali: skiing in winter, paragliding and zorbing in summer, the ropeway, distance from Manali and the best time to visit.

images.alt: Snow-covered slopes and the ropeway station at Solang Valley under snow peaks
images.caption: Solang Valley in winter

overview.text: Solang Valley, about 13 km from Manali, takes its name from the nearby village of Solang and 'nullah', a stream. It changes with the seasons: in winter its slopes are Manali's ski area, and in summer the meadows fill with paragliders and zorbing. A ropeway climbs above the valley for wide views of the snow peaks. Incredible India suggests April to June and September to January as the best times to visit; for snow, come between December and early March. Nearby, the Atal Tunnel leads on towards Lahaul, while Kothi village and the hot springs of Vashisht make easy stops on the way back to Manali.

places.name: Rohtang Pass

places.seoTitle: Rohtang Pass: Permits, Season & Atal Tunnel
places.seoDescription: Plan a Rohtang Pass trip from Manali: the online vehicle permit, when the road is open, altitude and weather, Rahala Falls and the Atal Tunnel.

images.alt: A road winding across high grassy slopes towards snow peaks near Rohtang Pass
images.caption: Near Rohtang Pass

overview.text:
Rohtang Pass, at 3,978 m on the Pir Panjal range about 51 km from Manali, links the green Kullu valley with the stark landscapes of Lahaul and Spiti. Snow closes the road from about November to May, and the pass is notorious for sudden snowstorms, so check the weather before you set out. Rahala Falls is on the way up.

Since October 2020, the 9.02-km Atal Tunnel has run beneath the pass, connecting Manali with Keylong.

items.title: Permits
items.body: Tourist vehicles need an online permit, issued against a daily quota set by the National Green Tribunal and the district. Permits are valid for one day, can be applied for up to two days ahead, and vehicles must be no more than 10 years old.

items.title: Season
items.body: The road over the pass is usually open from about May to November.

places.name: Vashisht
places.summary: A village 3 km from Manali with sulphurous hot springs and a Kath Kuni temple.
places.seoDescription: Vashisht near Manali: hot springs, bath timings and the temple of Sage Vashisht.

overview.text: Across the Beas, 3 km from Manali, the village of Vashisht is known for its sulphurous hot springs, with separate bathing areas, and its Kath Kuni-style temple of Sage Vashisht. The baths are listed as open 7 am–1 pm and 2 pm–9 pm daily. A trail leads on to Jogini Waterfall.

places.seoTitle: Naggar, Kullu Valley: Castle, Temples & Roerich Gallery

images.alt: A carved wooden balcony of Naggar Castle overlooking the misty Kullu valley
images.caption: Naggar Castle

overview.text:
Naggar, about 20 km from Manali, was once the seat of the Kullu kings. Naggar Castle, built around 1460 in the Kath Kuni style of alternating stone and timber, is now a heritage hotel with views over the Beas valley.

The village's temples include the Gauri Shankar Temple, with 12th-century stone carving, and the Tripura Sundari Temple, built of deodar wood. A 30-minute walk from the castle leads to the Nicholas Roerich Art Gallery, with the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute above it. Incredible India suggests September to November for pleasant weather.
